details:
hardhat-option@2.0.1 was published to npm on 2026-10-07 09:12 UTC and removed by npm on 2026-10-07 15:29 UTC. Like hardhat-promised@2.21.0 (published the day before), the name targets the Ethereum development tool hardhat, and the package is a copy of the pino logger (README badges still point to pino) with one file added that pino does not contain: lib/config.js, a 4,499,968-byte obfuscated script. index.js requires ./lib/config on line 6, so the payload runs as soon as the package is required. package.json carries the same fake author as hardhat-promised (Robert King <hello@jsonspack.com>), no repository, and the added dependency axios.

Behavior observed when lib/config.js is loaded in an instrumented sandbox: axios.post of JSON to http://167.88.172.33:8087/api/log containing os.hostname(), os.platform()/release()/type() and os.userInfo().username, with a fixed key ukey=309 (hardhat-promised uses 301), a tag t=3, a timestamp and a SHA-256 'validation' header. The messages posted are 'Failed to spawn autoUploadScript', 'Failed to spawn ldbScript' and 'Failed to spawn socketScript', which name the same three stealer modules as hardhat-promised: automatic file upload, LevelDB (browser extension / wallet storage) reading, and a persistent socket connection to the operator.

Trigger: on import (require). Type: trojanized copy of a popular library acting as an information-stealer loader with a hard-coded C2 at 167.88.172.33:8087; second package of the hardhat-promised family.
